project.name: careSync
project.summary: Spring Boot backend for a doctor/patient care platform: accounts and sessions, doctor and patient records, appointments with video consults and chat, lab-test bookings, Razorpay payments and refunds, and an AI assistant on Groq and Gemini. It is one deployable app on PostgreSQL, with Redis for caching, rate and quota counters, and Supabase S3 for files.

nodes.name: Client / User
nodes.description: Every browser and app that calls the API or opens the /ws STOMP socket. Allowed origins come from APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

evidence.note: app exposed directly on 8080, no proxy

nodes.name: Razorpay (webhook)
nodes.description: Razorpay posts signed payment events (payment.captured, payment.authorized, order.paid) when PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set and demo mode is off.

evidence.note: only enabled when not in demo mode and a secret is set

nodes.name: CorsFilter
nodes.description: Checks Origin against APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS and adds CORS headers, exposing Authorization and Content-Disposition.

nodes.name: RateLimitingFilter
nodes.description: In-memory per-IP token buckets: 5/min for OTP paths, 10/min for login/register/refresh and 20/min for /api/ai/*; over the limit it answers 429.

nodes.name: SecurityFilter (IP block)
nodes.description: Rejects requests from blocked client IPs with 403; skips /api/auth/ and /api/admin/ (login does its own IP check).

nodes.name: JwtAuthenticationFilter
nodes.description: Validates a Bearer JWT, loads the user and checks the server-side session is still live before setting the security context; with no token it passes the request on.

nodes.name: Authorization rules
nodes.description: URL rules (permitAll auth/webhook/public routes, role rules per prefix, anyRequest authenticated) plus @PreAuthorize on handlers; no login gives 401, a wrong role gives 403.

nodes.name: AuditTrailInterceptor
nodes.description: Spring MVC interceptor on /api/**: after each request to a patient-data or admin prefix it writes route template, record ids, status, user and IP to the audit log.

nodes.name: GlobalExceptionHandler
nodes.description: @RestControllerAdvice mapping AccessDenied (403), upload size, bad input, data and runtime exceptions to safe JSON errors.

nodes.name: StompAuthChannelInterceptor
nodes.description: Inbound STOMP channel interceptor that authenticates WebSocket frames before they reach @MessageMapping handlers.

nodes.name: Auth & sessions
nodes.description: AuthController with AuthenticationService, GoogleAuthService, SecurityService and TokenIssuer: login (admin second step by emailed code), register, Google sign-in, refresh, OTP and password reset, device sessions.

nodes.name: Doctors, patients & records
nodes.description: Doctor, Patient, MedicalHistory, Vital, LabTest, Feedback, SavedDoctor, DoctorLeave and FileUpload controllers with their services: profiles, medical history, vitals, lab-test catalogue, feedback and documents.

nodes.name: Appointments & video consults
nodes.description: Appointment, AppointmentAction and VideoConsultation controllers: slot holds, booking (with payment), state machine, SOAP drafts and sign-off, LiveKit video rooms.

nodes.name: Appointment chat (STOMP)
nodes.description: ChatController: receives /app/chat.sendMessage over the /ws socket, stores the message and broadcasts it on /topic/appointment/{id}; also serves chat history over REST.

nodes.name: Lab-test bookings
nodes.description: BookingController and BookingService: lab-test bookings by patients (with payment) and doctors, status changes and cancellation.

nodes.name: Payments & refunds
nodes.description: PaymentController with PaymentService, RazorpayService and PaymentRefundService: Razorpay checkout (or demo mode), verification, webhook settlement, refunds and earnings.

nodes.name: AI assistant
nodes.description: AiController and AiConversationController with AiService, the patient agent, doctor co-pilot, emergency triage, quota and conversation memory; calls Groq for chat and Gemini for vision and fallback.

nodes.name: Admin, analytics & reporting
nodes.description: Admin, Analytics, Reporting, Seeding and Master controllers: user and doctor moderation, IP blocks, sessions, audit logs, analytics, reports, seed data and master lists.

nodes.name: Notifications & email
nodes.description: NotificationController, NotificationService (stored notifications pushed to /user/queue/notifications) and EmailService (Resend HTTP first, SMTP fallback, logged to communications).

nodes.name: Scheduled jobs
nodes.description: In-process @Scheduled jobs: appointment reminders (every minute), no-show cleanup (15 min), stale checkout reconcile (5 min), due refunds (every minute) and nightly deactivation.

nodes.name: PostgreSQL
nodes.description: Primary store (JPA + Flyway migrations) for users, sessions, appointments, bookings, payments, records, audit and AI history. Address from SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL.

nodes.name: Redis
nodes.description: Spring cache (encrypted values, per-cache TTLs), slot locks, OTP and admin login codes, AI quota counters and AI conversation memory. Address from REDIS_HOST/REDIS_PORT.

nodes.name: Supabase S3 storage
nodes.description: Object storage for documents and images via the AWS S3 SDK, with presigned URLs for private files. Configured by SUPABASE_S3_* variables.

nodes.name: Razorpay API
nodes.description: Payment gateway: orders created, payments fetched and captured, refunds issued. Keys from RAZORPAY_KEY_ID / RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET.

nodes.name: Groq API
nodes.description: OpenAI-compatible chat completions (with tools and streaming) and model fallbacks for the AI assistant. Key from app.ai.groq.api-key.

nodes.name: Google Gemini API
nodes.description: Vision analysis of uploaded medical documents and certificates, and a text fallback for dictation. Key from GEMINI_API_KEY.

nodes.name: Resend email API
nodes.description: HTTP email provider tried first for transactional mail (OTP, admin login codes). Key from resend.api.key.

nodes.name: SMTP mail server
nodes.description: JavaMailSender fallback (or primary when MAIL_API_PROVIDER=smtp). Host from SPRING_MAIL_HOST.

nodes.name: Google OAuth tokeninfo
nodes.description: Verifies Google ID tokens for Google sign-in; audience checked against GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.

nodes.name: LiveKit Cloud
nodes.description: Video rooms for consultations: participant listing and room deletion through RoomServiceClient; join tokens are signed locally. Configured by LIVEKIT_URL / LIVEKIT_API_KEY.

flows.name: POST /api/auth/login
flows.summary: A user signs in with username and password; the backend checks IP block and lockout, verifies the password, records the attempt and starts a server-side session with JWT access and refresh tokens.

steps.action: The client posts credentials to the login endpoint.
Origin is checked against the allowed origins.
Login counts against the per-IP auth bucket of 10 requests per minute.
/api/auth/ paths skip the filter's IP block (login checks it itself).
No Bearer header, so JWT processing is skipped.
/api/auth/login is on the permitAll list.
AuthController passes the request, client IP and User-Agent to AuthenticationService.authenticate.
Blocked IPs and recent failed attempts for this username and IP are read.
The AuthenticationManager verifies the password against the stored hash.
The successful attempt, a new user session and a refresh token are saved.
Saved rows, including the new session id, are returned.
TokenIssuer signs an access JWT carrying the sessionId claim, and the response is built with both tokens and user data.
steps.data: accessToken, refreshToken, tokenType Bearer, user data

steps.action: CORS headers are added, exposing Authorization.
The client receives the tokens.

branches.label: Too many login attempts (429)
branches.condition: The IP has used its 10 auth requests this minute

outcome.description: Rejected by the rate limiter before reaching the controller.

steps.action: The bucket is empty, so the filter writes a 429 JSON error and stops the chain.
CORS headers are still applied.
The client receives the 429.

branches.label: Wrong password or locked (400)
branches.condition: Password check fails, or the account/IP is locked or blocked

outcome.description: Failed attempt recorded; generic error returned.

steps.action: The failure is recorded as a login attempt and rethrown as a generic message; the controller returns 400.
CORS headers are added.
The client receives the 400 error.

outcome.description: No tokens yet; the admin must post the code to /api/auth/login/verify-code.

steps.action: A one-time login code is stored under a challenge id with a TTL.
The code is handed to EmailService for delivery.
EmailService tries the Resend HTTP provider first.
Resend accepts the email.
The send result is returned to the caller.
A response with mfaRequired and the challenge id (no tokens) is built.
CORS headers are added.
The client shows the code prompt.

flows.name: POST /api/bookings/patient/with-payment
flows.summary: A patient books lab tests and starts payment: the booking is saved as PENDING, PaymentService creates a payment row and a Razorpay order, and the client gets checkout details.

steps.action: The patient posts the selected tests and the payment request.
Origin is checked.
The client IP is checked against active IP blocks.
The Bearer JWT is validated, the user loaded and the session confirmed live.
The request must be authenticated and @PreAuthorize requires role PATIENT.
BookingController calls BookingService.createBookingWithPayment.
The patient and tests are loaded, the total priced and a PENDING booking saved.
The amount must equal the booking total; then the payment request goes to PaymentService.
Outside demo mode, startCheckout validates the target and creates the payment record.
A Razorpay order is created for the amount in paise.
Razorpay returns the order id.
The order id is saved on the payment and checkout details built.
The booking response carries the transaction id, payment status and checkout.
@CacheEvict clears ANALYTICS:OVERALL and the patient's PATIENT:FINANCIAL entry.
The controller returns 201 Created.
After completion the route, record ids, status, user and IP are written to the audit log.
CORS headers are added.
The client opens Razorpay checkout with the returned order.

branches.label: No or expired login (401)
branches.condition: No valid Bearer token or the session has ended

outcome.description: Rejected by Spring Security before the controller.

steps.action: No usable token, so no authentication is set.
The authentication entry point answers 401.
CORS headers are added.
The client refreshes the token or asks the user to sign in again.

branches.label: Payment cannot start (400)
branches.condition: Razorpay keys missing, order creation fails, or amount/target invalid

outcome.description: Booking stays PENDING so the patient can retry payment.

steps.action: startCheckout throws (for example Razorpay is not configured).
The service wraps it as Payment failed and the controller answers 400.
The refused request is still audited with its status.
CORS headers are added.
The client shows the error.

flows.notes: With PAYMENT_DEMO_MODE on (the compose default), PaymentService takes the demo path instead of calling Razorpay (PaymentService.java:130-150). Settlement happens later through POST /api/payments/razorpay/verify or the Razorpay webhook.

flows.name: POST /api/payments/webhook/razorpay
flows.summary: Razorpay reports a captured payment; the backend verifies the signature, locks the payment row, re-fetches the payment from Razorpay, settles it and completes the booking.

steps.action: Razorpay posts a signed event.
The request enters the filter chain; a server-to-server call has no browser Origin, so CORS has nothing to check.
The caller IP is checked against active IP blocks.
POST /api/payments/webhook/razorpay is permitAll.
The controller checks webhooks are enabled, then the HMAC signature is verified.
The payment for the Razorpay order id is locked for update.
steps.data: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE by order id

steps.action: The body is only trusted for ids; the payment is re-fetched from Razorpay.
payments.fetch is called.
Razorpay returns the payment entity.
settle checks order and amount, and captures an authorized payment.
The payment is saved as SUCCESS and a PENDING booking becomes COMPLETED.
The controller answers 200 status success.
The /api/payments request is written to the audit log.
The response leaves through the filter chain.
Razorpay receives the acknowledgement.

branches.label: Webhooks disabled (404)
branches.condition: Demo mode on or PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET not set

outcome.description: Webhook endpoint answers 404 when not enabled.

steps.action: isWebhookConfigured is false, so the controller answers 404.
The request is audited.
The response leaves through the filter chain.
Razorpay receives 404.

branches.label: Invalid signature (401)
branches.condition: X-Razorpay-Signature does not match the HMAC of the body

steps.action: SecurityException is caught and the controller answers 401.
The refused request is audited.
The response leaves through the filter chain.
Razorpay receives 401.

flows.notes: The rate limiter (not a limited path) and the JWT filter (no Bearer header) do nothing for this request, so they are not shown as steps. CORS appears only as the chain's entry and exit.

flows.name: POST /api/ai/chat
flows.summary: A patient chats with the AI assistant: rule-based emergency triage, conversation memory from Redis, the Groq tool-calling agent with a per-user quota, then memory, chat history and an AI audit record are saved.

steps.action: The user posts a chat message.
Origin is checked.
The request counts against the per-IP AI bucket of 20 per minute.
The client IP is checked against active IP blocks.
The Bearer JWT and session are validated.
/api/ai/chat requires role PATIENT or DOCTOR.
AiService.getResponse runs rule-based emergency triage for patients (no AI).
Recent conversation history is read (stored encrypted).
The patient agent calls Groq with tools; each model call first consumes the user's AI quota.
Per-minute and per-day quota counters are incremented with a TTL.
The chat-completions request is sent to Groq.
Groq runs the model (with configured fallback models).
Groq returns tool calls or the final text.
Requested tools are executed on the server as this patient.
Tools query data such as matching doctors.
Rows are returned to the tool.
The agent's final reply (text, optional booking card, emergency notice) is assembled and the turn saved to memory.
The conversation memory is written back, encrypted, with a TTL.
The turn is recorded in saved chat history and an AI audit record is logged.
Conversation, message and AI audit rows are saved.
The controller returns 200 with the response.
The /api/ai request is written to the audit log.
CORS headers are added.
The client renders the reply.

branches.label: Emergency detected by rules
branches.condition: A patient's message matches red-flag rules

steps.action: An emergency response is built without calling the model, then the turn is saved to memory.

branches.label: AI allowance used up
branches.condition: The per-minute or per-day quota is exceeded

outcome.description: success=false with a friendly message; failure audited.

steps.action: AiQuotaExceededException is caught, logged to AI audit, and a friendly message returned.
The request is audited.
CORS headers are added.
The client shows the allowance message.

branches.label: Too many AI requests (429)
branches.condition: The IP used its 20 AI requests this minute

steps.action: The AI bucket is empty, so the filter answers 429.
CORS headers are added.
The client receives the 429.

flows.notes: Traced for a patient. Doctors go through DoctorCopilotService (AiService.java:163) instead, falling back to a basic assistant on error. The streaming variant POST /api/ai/chat/stream shares getResponse but replies as server-sent events.

flows.name: GET /api/doctors/{id}
flows.summary: A doctor or admin reads a doctor profile; DoctorService serves it from the encrypted Redis cache DOCTOR:PROFILE (1h TTL) or loads it from PostgreSQL and caches it.

steps.action: The client requests a doctor profile by id.
Origin is checked.
The client IP is checked against active IP blocks.
The Bearer JWT and session are validated.
/api/doctors/** allows DOCTOR, PATIENT or ADMIN at URL level.
@PreAuthorize narrows the handler to DOCTOR or ADMIN, which calls getDoctorDtoById.
@Cacheable looks up DOCTOR:PROFILE id_{id} (miss on the main path).
On a miss the method body runs and queries the repository.
The doctor row is selected by id.
The doctor row is returned.
The entity is mapped to DoctorDto with stats.
The DTO is cached encrypted with a 1 hour TTL.
The DTO is filtered for the current viewer and returned with 200.
CORS headers are added.
The client renders the profile.
The cached, decrypted DTO is returned and PostgreSQL is skipped.
The empty result becomes 404 Not Found.
CORS headers are added.
The client receives 404.

branches.label: Patient caller (403)
branches.condition: The caller is a PATIENT (allowed by the URL rule but not by @PreAuthorize)

steps.action: @PreAuthorize rejects the PATIENT role and throws AccessDeniedException.
GlobalExceptionHandler maps it to 403 with a generic body.
CORS headers are added.
The client receives 403.

flows.notes: /api/doctors is not an audited prefix, so AuditTrailInterceptor writes nothing for this request (AuditTrailInterceptor.java:32).

skipped: Frontend: src/main/resources/templates (server-side email templates), not analyzed
Flows not traced: appointment booking and state machine, video consult token/status/end, file upload to S3, STOMP chat, Google sign-in, refresh/logout, scheduled jobs, admin endpoints
limitations: Single deployable Spring Boot app with no gateway: compose exposes port 8080 directly (docker-compose.yml:33). Service nodes are modules grouped from controllers and their services, not separate deployables.

RateLimitingFilter, SecurityFilter and JwtAuthenticationFilter are all added before UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter (SecurityConfig.java:116-118). The chain shows them in registration order, assuming Spring keeps insertion order for filters anchored the same way. CORS is assumed to run first, as Spring Security places CorsFilter.
The Security filter chain and AuditTrailInterceptor are shared by every REST module. Their owner is set to auth-module by convention, and the last link fans out to each module.
AuditTrailInterceptor acts only in afterCompletion, so flows show it on the response side only.
The Razorpay webhook is active only when demo mode is off and PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set. The compose default PAYMENT_DEMO_MODE=true sends payments down the demo path, with no Razorpay calls.
NotificationService and ChatController push to clients over the in-memory STOMP broker (/user/queue/notifications, /topic/appointment/{id}). These server-to-client pushes are not drawn as edges.
Endpoint lists were taken from class- and method-level mapping annotations; no runtime context path is configured. GET /api/master/** is public; other /api/master methods require ADMIN.
app.file.upload.path and the app_uploads volume are declared (application.properties:46, docker-compose.yml:95), but no Java code reading the path was found.
No Kubernetes files: hosts, replicas and the Redis/Supabase/LiveKit deployments come from env variable names only.

Renderer warning left on purpose: the webhook flow enters and leaves the filter chain at CorsFilter (razorpay-webhook <-> cors-mw). Its only edge goes to the payments service, as the schema requires for external callers.
